requirements.requirement: Provision local accounts designer, reviewer, and visitor.
requirements.summary: All three local accounts were absent initially, created successfully, resolved before restart, and persisted after restart.

requirements.requirement: Automatically grant reviewer read/write access to new designer-created subdirectories and documents while retaining designer ownership.
requirements.summary: Default ACLs were configured on the project directory. Direct tests before and after restart showed designer-created directories and documents remained designer-owned, inherited reviewer permissions, and allowed reviewer reads and appends.

requirements.requirement: Ensure visitor has no access to the project area and newly inherited content.
requirements.summary: The parent and inherited ACLs explicitly deny visitor. Identity-based tests demonstrated denial of document reads, writes, directory listing, and creation at the project root, including after restart.
The existing brief.txt retained its baseline SHA-256 hash, root ownership, mode 0644, length, and timestamp. Final directory listings showed that temporary test artifacts had been removed.

requirements.requirement: Provide persistent filesystem inheritance without a periodic permission-repair job.
requirements.summary: Access and default POSIX ACLs provide creation-time inheritance, and their behavior persisted across a verified restart. The bounded scheduler inspection found no task-related cron entry or systemd unit.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remained unchanged. ACL tooling came from the native RHEL BaseOS repository and remained functional after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct pre- and post-restart behavior proves persistent ACL inheritance, reviewer read/write access, designer ownership, visitor denial, preserved data, persistent accounts, and unchanged platform release/kernel. The node-restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, acknowledged restart, a different post-restart identity, and recovered service, data, and access behavior; fixed lifecycle observations independently corroborate the boot change.
limitations: The negative scheduler check covered standard cron directories and task-related systemd unit-file names, but was not an exhaustive content search of every possible scheduler configuration. The direct default-ACL implementation and restart test nevertheless establish that periodic repair is unnecessary.

Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory the project tree, accounts, or installed ACL package; those outcomes rely on the detailed executor commands. The lifecycle data independently corroborates platform stability, restart identity, service health, socket exposure, and package-manager health.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified in the chronological command trace. Package installation and its libacl dependency upgrade enabled the required ACL implementation; account creation and ACL changes directly implemented the task. Functional-test files were bounded evidence artifacts and were removed. The restart was required by the provider protocol. Final observations show no failed services, no unexpected listeners, healthy package management, and only normal reboot-related temporary-file and PID changes.
